title: Establishment of a new genus for Cyclograpsus escondidensis Rathbun in Glassell, 1933 within the family Sesarmidae Dana, 1851 (Decapoda: Brachyura)
content:
Abstract
The rare species Cyclograpsus escondidensis Rathbun in Glassell, 1933, known only from the Gulf of California, was compared with other species of Cyclograpsus H. Milne Edwards, 1837, as well as with other American sesarmids, using morphological (including a 3D model) and molecular phylogenetic analyses. Molecular analyses based on fragments of two mitochondrial genes (COI, 16S) and one nuclear gene (28S) further support the view that the sesarmids Sesarma Say, 1817 and Armases Abele, 1992, as well as the varunid Cyclograpsus, H. Milne Edwards, 1837 are paraphyletic in their current composition. Unexpectedly, C. escondidensis was recovered within the Sesarmidae clade rather than among Varunidae. As a result, C. escondidensis must now be placed in a new genus in Sesarmidae Dana, 1851. Schubarma gen. nov. is formally established for C. escondidensis based on unique characters that distinguish it from both the phylogenetically closest Sesarma and the morphologically most similar Cyclorma from Djibouti. These unique characters include those of cephalothorax, carapace, ambulatory legs, and male first gonopod (G1).
